title: Place each fact in the ICF model
context: The WHO's International Classification of Functioning (ICF) uses these terms to describe disability.
question: Is each fact an impairment, an activity limitation or a participation restriction?

parts.label: Impairment
parts.definition: A problem in how a part of the body or mind works, or in its structure.

parts.label: Activity limitation
parts.definition: Difficulty doing a task or action, such as walking, reading or gripping.

parts.label: Participation restriction
parts.definition: A problem taking part in life, such as work, study, travel or time with friends.

workedExample: Rosa's legs are paralysed after a spinal cord injury.
Rosa can't get to team meetings, which are upstairs in a building with no lift.
cases: Ana has low vision from glaucoma.
Ana can't read standard-size print.
Ana can't sit the paper-only licensing exam her job requires.
Ben has profound hearing loss in both ears.
Ben can't follow speech on a phone call.
Ben is left out of his team's weekly phone meetings.
Chloe has rheumatoid arthritis in her hands.
Chloe can't grip and lift heavy boxes.
Chloe gave up volunteering at the food bank, where the work is packing boxes.
Emi has dyslexia, which affects how her brain processes written words.
Emi reads long documents much more slowly than most people.
Emi misses out on promotion because the assessment is a timed written test.
Farid has epilepsy, and medication doesn't fully control his seizures.
Farid can't drive.
Farid can't take the field sales job he was offered, which needs a driving licence.
Grace has memory loss after a brain injury.
Grace can't remember a list of spoken instructions.
Grace had to step down as the shift manager at her café.
Hugo has a tremor in both hands from Parkinson's disease.
Hugo can't tap small targets on a touchscreen accurately.
Hugo can't buy tickets at his station, which has only touchscreen machines.
Ines has chronic fatigue syndrome, which leaves her with very little energy.
Ines can't stand for more than ten minutes.
Ines can't work her shifts on the supermarket checkout, where staff stand.
Jamal has red-green colour blindness.
Jamal can't tell red status lights from green ones.
Jamal can't train as a train driver, a job that requires full colour vision.
Kai has a stammer.
Kai can't speak quickly under time pressure.
Kai is turned down for a call-centre job after a timed phone interview.
